item.title: Esther Rantzen now ‘too physically fragile’ to end her life in Switzerland
item.description: Broadcaster, 86, had intended to end her life in Swiss clinic after being diagnosed with terminal lung cancer in 2023 Esther Rantzen has said she is no longer able to travel to Switzerland to end her life because she has become “too physically fragile”. Rantzen, who presented the TV current affairs programme That’s Life! for 21 years and founded the youth support charity Childline, had intended to end her life in a Dignitas assisted dying clinic in Switzerland after being diagnosed with terminal lung cancer in 2023. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Teen Uses Cancer Game: Daniel Zhang turns Tumor Tactics into learning tool; reaches 1,500 K-8 students
item.description: In an innovative step, a San Diego teenager named Daniel Zhang crafted Tumor Tactics, an educational game designed to demystify cancer for young minds. Motivated by his grandmother's battle with the illness, Daniel aims to make intricate cancer biology accessible to children. His project has garnered funding and will be showcased at the United Nations Science Summit, alongside his role in STEAMLabs International, where he promotes STEM and arts education. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Atentados del 11-S: publican informes que revelan conocimiento de toxicidad del aire tras ataques
item.description: 25 años después del atentado a las torres gemelas, la sombra de la tragedia aún flota sobre Nueva York. El alcalde, Zohran Mamdani, reveló documentos que demuestran que las autoridades tenían conocimiento de la toxicidad del aire incluso meses después de la tragedia, a pesar de que habían asegurado a los neoyorquinos que era seguro volver a la zona. Los datos de seguimiento médico evidencian que, tras el ataque, las muertes por cánceres y otras enfermedades relacionadas con la contaminación se triplicaron. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: A cellular threshold can determine whether herpesvirus becomes active or lies dormant
item.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we wore masks and kept 2 meters (6.6 feet) apart in an effort to reduce the spread of the tiny droplets we release into the air with every breath, conversation or cough. The main goal was to reduce the number of virus particles—known as virions—to which we were exposed. For each virus, a person must be exposed to a minimum infectious dose to develop disease, and in many cases, the larger the dose, the more severe the illness. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: More than 1,000 children dead in Bangladesh measles crisis
item.description: The death toll from measles in Bangladesh topped 1,000 children since March, health officials said on Wednesday, admitting that failures in a vaccination drive could have fuelled the outbreak. The South Asian nation of 170 million has recorded 1,002 deaths and 187,484 infections among children, making this year’s outbreak the country’s deadliest in decades, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). item.title: Indonesia has new food safety rules for free meals. Why are students still falling ill?
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s flagship free nutritious meals programme is facing renewed scrutiny after yet another wave of mass food poisoning that affected more than 2,000 students, raising questions about why safeguards on paper fail to translate to food safety on the ground. A series of illnesses were reported in Java, Sumatra, and Sulawesi in the past week. The latest was on Tuesday in Rembang, Central Java, where 200 students of an Islamic school showed symptoms of food poisoning... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
